question.prompt:
The number \(N\) is a two-digit number with the following properties:

When \(N\) is divided by \(9,\) the remainder is \(1.\)
 
When \(N\) is divided by \(10,\) the remainder is \(3.\)

What is the remainder when \(N\) is divided by \(11?\)

solutions.explanation:
A remainder of \(3\) upon division by \(10\) means that the ones digit is \(3\). Since \(N\) has two digits, all possibilities are
\[
13,23,33,43,53,63,73,83,93.
\]
A remainder of \(1\) upon division by \(9\) means that \(N-1\) is a multiple of \(9\). Subtracting \(1\) from the candidates gives
\[
12,22,32,42,52,62,72,82,92.
\]
Only \(72=9\cdot8\) is a multiple of \(9\), so \(N=73\). Finally,
\[
73=11\cdot6+7.
\]
Because \(0\le7<11\), the requested remainder is \(7\), choice E.
solutions.title: List the possible numbers
